ko.title: 3.4% 성장, 그런데 왜 체감은 더 둔하게 느껴질까? 3분기 GDP 보고서 읽기

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 미국

segments.src: economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% in the second.
segments.tr: 경제는 3분기에 연율 3.4% 성장하여 2분기의 2.2%에서 상승했습니다.

segments.src: By the usual yardsticks, that is a solid number.
segments.tr: 일반적인 잣대로 보면 이는 견조한 숫자입니다.

segments.src: Yet plenty of households say they feel no stronger, because grocery bills, rent, insurance and borrowing costs still weigh on their budgets.
segments.tr: 하지만 식비, 월세, 보험료 및 대출 비용이 여전히 가계 예산에 부담을 주고 있기 때문에 많은 가구가 사정이 나아졌다고 느끼지 못한다고 말합니다.

segments.src: Both things can be true.
segments.tr: 두 가지 모두 사실일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: GDP and a family's finances measure different things.
segments.tr: GDP와 한 가계의 재정 상태는 서로 다른 것을 측정합니다.

segments.src: This article looks at what the headline figure captures, what tends to drive it, and why it can diverge from everyday experience.
segments.tr: 이 기사에서는 헤드라인 수치가 무엇을 담아내는지, 무엇이 이를 견인하는 경향이 있는지, 그리고 왜 이것이 일상적인 체감과 달라질 수 있는지 살펴봅니다.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *본 기사는 일반적인 정보 제공만을 목적으로 합니다.

segments.src: It is not investment, tax or financial advice.*
segments.tr: 투자, 세무 또는 금융 자문이 아닙니다.*

segments.src: ## What the 3.4% Actually Means
segments.tr: ## 3.4%가 실제로 의미하는 바

segments.src: Gross domestic product is the total value of goods and services produced in the country over a period.
segments.tr: 국내총생산(GDP)은 일정 기간 동안 한 국가 내에서 생산된 재화와 서비스의 총가치입니다.

segments.src: Government statisticians report the quarterly change as an **annualized** rate.
segments.tr: 정부 통계학자들은 분기별 변화율을 **연율**로 발표합니다.

segments.src: That is the pace the economy would reach if the quarter's growth continued for a full year.
segments.tr: 이는 해당 분기의 성장이 1년 내내 지속될 경우 경제가 도달하게 될 속도입니다.

segments.src: A 3.4% reading does not mean the economy grew 3.4% in three months.
segments.tr: 3.4%라는 수치가 경제가 3개월 동안 3.4% 성장했다는 의미는 아닙니다.

segments.src: It means it expanded at a pace that, sustained, would add up to 3.4% over twelve months.
segments.tr: 이 속도가 유지될 경우 12개월 동안 총 3.4% 확장하는 속도로 성장했음을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Three features of the figure matter for interpretation:
segments.tr: 이 수치를 해석할 때는 세 가지 특징이 중요합니다.

segments.src: - **It is an early estimate.** The first reading is based on incomplete data and is usually revised as more information arrives. Revisions can be meaningful.
segments.tr: - **초기 추정치(속보치)입니다.** 첫 번째 수치는 불완전한 데이터를 기반으로 하며, 더 많은 정보가 들어옴에 따라 보통 수정됩니다. 수정치는 상당한 수준일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **It is adjusted for inflation.** The headline is "real" GDP. It strips out price changes to show changes in output.
segments.tr: - **인플레이션이 반영(조정)된 수치입니다.** 헤드라인은 "실질" GDP입니다. 가격 변화를 제거하여 산출량의 변화만을 보여줍니다.

segments.src: - **It is an aggregate.** It tells you how big the total pie grew. It does not tell you who got the larger slices.
segments.tr: - **합계(집계치)입니다.** 전체 파이가 얼마나 커졌는지를 알려줄 뿐, 누가 더 큰 조각을 가져갔는지는 알려주지 않습니다.

segments.src: The acceleration from 2.2% to 3.4% suggests momentum improved.
segments.tr: 2.2%에서 3.4%로의 가속화는 성장 모멘텀이 개선되었음을 시사합니다.

segments.src: Quarterly figures can be noisy, though, and analysts often look at several quarters together before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: 하지만 분기별 수치는 변동성이 클 수 있으므로 분석가들은 결론을 내리기 전에 여러 분기를 함께 들여다보는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: ## The Main Drivers
segments.tr: ## 주요 견인 요인

segments.src: GDP is built from a few components: consumer spending, business investment, government spending, and net trade.
segments.tr: GDP는 소비 지출, 기업 투자, 정부 지출, 순수출의 몇 가지 요소로 구성됩니다.

segments.src: Which of these moved most is usually the key to understanding a quarter.
segments.tr: 이 중 어떤 요소가 가장 크게 움직였는지가 보통 특정 분기를 이해하는 핵심 열쇠가 됩니다.

segments.src: ### Consumers
segments.tr: ### 소비

segments.src: Household spending is the largest piece of the economy, typically well over half of GDP.
segments.tr: 가계 지출은 경제에서 가장 큰 비중을 차지하며, 보통 GDP의 절반을 훨씬 넘습니다.

segments.src: When consumers keep buying services such as travel, health care and dining out, as well as goods, growth tends to hold up.
segments.tr: 소비자가 상품뿐만 아니라 여행, 의료, 외식 등 서비스 지출을 계속 유지할 때 성장은 잘 버티는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: Strong spending does not always mean households are comfortable, however.
segments.tr: 그러나 지출이 견조하다고 해서 가계의 사정이 항상 넉넉하다는 뜻은 아닙니다.

segments.src: Some of it can reflect higher-income households spending freely.
segments.tr: 일부는 고소득 가구가 아낌없이 지출하는 것을 반영할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Some can reflect people drawing down savings or leaning on credit to keep up with higher prices.
segments.tr: 일부는 오른 물가를 감당하기 위해 저축을 꺼내 쓰거나 신용에 의존하는 것을 반영할 수도 있습니다.

segments.src: ### AI-Related Investment
segments.tr: ### AI 관련 투자

segments.src: Business investment has drawn particular attention because of heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
segments.tr: 인공지능 인프라에 대한 대규모 지출로 인해 기업 투자가 특히 주목받고 있습니다.

segments.src: Data centers, computing hardware, software and the power and construction work that support them all count as investment in GDP.
segments.tr: 데이터 센터, 컴퓨팅 하드웨어, 소프트웨어, 그리고 이를 뒷받침하는 전력 및 건설 작업은 모두 GDP에서 투자로 집계됩니다.

segments.src: This spending can lift the headline figure noticeably.
segments.tr: 이 이러한 지출은 헤드라인 수치를 눈에 띄게 끌어올릴 수 있습니다.

segments.src: It is also concentrated in a relatively small number of companies and industries.
segments.tr: 또한 이는 상대적으로 소수의 기업과 산업에 집중되어 있습니다.

segments.src: A boom in server and data-center building can raise GDP without immediately changing the experience of a typical worker or renter.
segments.tr: 서버 및 데이터 센터 건설 붐은 일반 근로자나 세입자의 일상적 체감을 즉시 바꾸지 않으면서도 GDP를 끌어올릴 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ### Trade
segments.tr: ### 무역

segments.src: Net exports are one of the more volatile pieces of the report.
segments.tr: 순수출은 보고서에서 변동성이 가장 큰 요소 중 하나입니다.

segments.src: Imports subtract from GDP and exports add to it.
segments.tr: 수입은 GDP에서 차감되고 수출은 더해집니다.

segments.src: Swings in shipping, tariffs, inventory decisions and timing can move this component sharply from one quarter to the next.
segments.tr: 물동량, 관세, 재고 결정 및 시점의 변동은 한 분기에서 다음 분기로 이 요소를 크게 움직일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: A big shift in trade can make the headline number look stronger or weaker than the underlying demand.
segments.tr: 무역의 큰 변동은 헤드라인 수치를 기초 수요보다 더 강하거나 약해 보이게 만들 수 있습니다.

segments.src: For that reason, many economists also watch measures that strip out trade and inventories to get a cleaner read on domestic demand.
segments.tr: 그러한 이유로 많은 경제학자들은 국내 수요를 더 명확하게 파악하기 위해 무역과 재고를 제외한 지표도 주시합니다.

segments.src: ### Government and Inventories
segments.tr: ### 정부 지출 및 재고

segments.src: Government spending and changes in business inventories also contribute.
segments.tr: 정부 지출과 기업 재고의 변화도 기여합니다.

segments.src: Inventory swings in particular tend to reverse, so they can flatter one quarter and drag on the next.
segments.tr: 특히 재고 변동은 반전되는 경향이 있으므로 한 분기를 돋보이게 만들었다가 다음 분기에는 걸림돌이 될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Why It Can Still Feel Slower
segments.tr: ## 왜 여전히 더 둔하게 느껴질 수 있는가

segments.src: If output is rising at a healthy clip, why do so many people feel stuck?
segments.tr: 산출량이 순조롭게 늘어나고 있다면, 왜 이렇게 많은 사람들이 제자리걸음을 하고 있다고 느낄까요?

segments.src: Several explanations are commonly offered by economists.
segments.tr: 경제학자들은 일반적으로 몇 가지 설명을 제시합니다.

segments.src: Prices rise even when inflation cools.** Inflation measures how fast prices increase.
segments.tr: 인플레이션이 둔화되더라도 가격은 계속 상승합니다.** 인플레이션은 물가가 얼마나 빠르게 오르는지를 측정합니다.

segments.src: A slowing rate does not mean prices fall.
segments.tr: 상승률이 낮아진다고 해서 물가가 떨어지는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: If the cost of food, housing or insurance jumped in earlier years, those higher levels remain.
segments.tr: 지난 몇 년 동안 식료품, 주거비, 보험료의 비용이 크게 올랐다면 그 높은 수준은 그대로 유지됩니다.

segments.src: Households tend to judge the economy by the prices they see now, not by the pace of change.
segments.tr: 가계는 변화의 속도가 아니라 현재 눈에 보이는 물가 수준으로 경제를 판단하는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: Essentials weigh more than averages suggest.** Official inflation gauges average across many goods.
segments.tr: 필수품의 비중은 평균이 시사하는 것보다 큽니다.** 공식 인플레이션 지표는 많은 재화의 평균을 냅니다.

segments.src: A household that spends a large share of its income on rent, groceries, childcare or health care may experience its own inflation rate as higher than the average.
segments.tr: 소득의 큰 부분을 월세, 식료품, 보육비 또는 의료비에 지출하는 가구는 체감 인플레이션율이 평균보다 높다고 느낄 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Borrowing remains expensive.** Even if interest rates have eased from their peaks, mortgage, auto and credit-card costs can be well above where they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: 대출 금리가 여전히 비쌉니다.** 금리가 고점에서 하락했더라도 주택담보대출, 자동차 할부, 신용카드 비용은 몇 년 전보다 훨씬 높은 수준일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: That limits what many households can afford, whatever the national growth rate says.
segments.tr: 이는 국가 성장률이 어떠하든 많은 가구가 감당할 수 있는 능력을 제한합니다.

segments.src: Growth is not evenly shared.** An economy can expand while gains flow mostly to business owners, investors and higher earners.
segments.tr: 성장 혜택이 고르게 분배되지 않습니다.** 경제 혜택의 대부분이 사업주, 투자자, 고소득자에게 흘러가는 동안에도 경제는 확장될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Wage growth that merely keeps pace with prices leaves little sense of progress.
segments.tr: 물가 상승률을 겨우 따라가는 수준의 임금 인상은 체감되는 살림살이 개선을 느끼기 어렵게 합니다.

segments.src: Jobs and confidence are separate from output.** Growth can be strong while hiring slows or workers worry about job security.
segments.tr: 일자리와 심리는 산출량과 별개입니다.** 채용이 줄어들거나 근로자가 고용 불안을 느끼는 동안에도 성장은 강력할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Perceptions of the labor market often shape sentiment more than GDP does.
segments.tr: 노동 시장에 대한 인식이 GDP보다 경제 심리를 형성하는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: GDP is not a measure of well-being.** It counts production, not savings, debt, housing affordability or financial stress.
segments.tr: GDP는 삶의 질이나 웰빙을 측정하는 지표가 아닙니다.** GDP는 생산을 집계할 뿐 저축, 부채, 주거 affordability(감당 가능성)나 재정적 스트레스는 측정하지 않습니다.

segments.src: A country can post strong GDP while many individuals feel squeezed.
segments.tr: 많은 개인들이 팍팍함을 느끼는 와중에도 한 국가의 GDP는 강력하게 나타날 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 향후 주시해야 할 사항

segments.src: A single quarter does not settle the question.
segments.tr: 단 하나의 분기 결과로 결론을 내릴 수는 없습니다.

segments.src: These indicators can help put the 3.4% figure in context:
segments.tr: 다음 지표들은 3.4%라는 수치를 맥락 속에서 이해하는 데 도움이 될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Revisions to the GDP estimate**, which can change the story.
segments.tr: - **GDP 추정치의 수정치**: 전체적인 맥락을 바꿀 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Real disposable income**, meaning income after taxes and inflation, which says more about household capacity than GDP does.
segments.tr: - **실질 가처분 소득**: 세금과 인플레이션을 차감한 소득으로, GDP보다 가계의 여력에 대해 더 많은 것을 알려줍니다.

segments.src: - **Wage growth compared with price growth**, since the gap between the two determines whether paychecks stretch further.
segments.tr: - **물가 상승률 대비 임금 상승률**: 이 두 가지의 격차가 실질 구매력 향상 여부를 결정합니다.

segments.src: - **Labor market data**, including hiring, unemployment and job openings.
segments.tr: - **노동 시장 데이터**: 채용, 실업률, 구인 건수 등을 포함합니다.

segments.src: - **Business investment outside the AI sector**, to see whether growth is broad or narrow.
segments.tr: - **AI 부문 외의 기업 투자**: 성장이 광범위한지 아니면 좁은 분야에 국한되어 있는지를 확인할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Consumer sentiment surveys**, which capture how people feel, not only what they spend.
segments.tr: - **소비자심리지수 조사**: 사람들이 얼마를 쓰는지뿐만 아니라 어떻게 느끼는지를 담아냅니다.

segments.src: ## A Practical Takeaway for Households
segments.tr: ## 가계를 위한 실용적인 시사점

segments.src: National statistics are useful for understanding the economy's direction.
segments.tr: 국가 통계는 경제의 방향을 이해하는 데 유용합니다.

segments.src: They are a poor guide to your own situation.
segments.tr: 하지만 개인의 상황을 판단하기에는 부족한 지침입니다.

segments.src: A few general habits can help you separate the headlines from your own finances:
segments.tr: 몇 가지 일반적인 습관을 통해 헤드라인 뉴스 economics와 자신의 재정 상태를 분리해 볼 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - Track your own budget, especially the categories that have risen fastest.
segments.tr: - 자신의 가계부 예산, 특히 가장 빠르게 오른 지출 항목을 점검하세요.

segments.src: - Compare your income growth with the prices you actually pay.
segments.tr: - 자신의 소득 증가율을 실제 지불하는 물가와 비교해 보세요.

segments.src: - Review variable-rate debt and think about what a change in rates would mean for you.
segments.tr: - 변동금리 부채를 검토하고 금리 변화가 자신에게 어떤 의미일지 생각해 보세요.

segments.src: - Keep an emergency cushion if you can, since a strong economy does not guarantee job stability.
segments.tr: - 견조한 경제가 일자리의 안정을 보장하지는 않으므로 가능한 비상 자금을 마련해 두세요.

segments.src: - Treat any single data release as one data point, not a forecast.
segments.tr: - 단일 데이터 발표는 예측이 아닌 하나의 데이터 포인트로 취급하세요.

segments.src: ## Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 결론

segments.src: A 3.4% annualized growth rate points to an economy with real momentum, helped by consumer spending, heavy AI-related investment and shifts in trade.
segments.tr: 연율 3.4%의 성장률은 소비 지출, 대규모 AI 관련 투자 및 무역 변동에 힘입어 실질적인 모멘텀을 가진 경제를 가리킵니다.

segments.src: But GDP measures total output.
segments.tr: 하지만 GDP는 총산출량을 측정합니다.

segments.src: It does not measure how comfortable families feel after paying for housing, food and debt.
segments.tr: 주거비, 식비, 부채 상환 후 가계가 얼마나 여유롭게 느끼는지는 측정하지 못합니다.

segments.src: The gap between a strong headline and a tight household budget is not a contradiction.
segments.tr: 강력한 헤드라인 지표와 팍팍한 가계 예산 사이의 격차는 모순이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It reflects the difference between how much an economy produces and how that production, and the price of living, show up in daily life.

zh.title: 3.4% 的增长，为什么感觉依然放缓？解读第三季度 GDP 报告

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 美国

segments.src: economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% in the second.
segments.tr: 经济在第三季度按年率计算增长了 3.4%，高于第二季度的 2.2%。

segments.src: By the usual yardsticks, that is a solid number.
segments.tr: 按通常的标准来看，这是一个坚实的数据。

segments.src: Yet plenty of households say they feel no stronger, because grocery bills, rent, insurance and borrowing costs still weigh on their budgets.
segments.tr: 然而，许多家庭表示他们并没有感到经济变得更强劲，因为食品杂货账单、租金、保险和借贷成本依然压在他们的预算上。

segments.src: Both things can be true.
segments.tr: 这两种情况可以同时成立。

segments.src: GDP and a family's finances measure different things.
segments.tr: GDP 和家庭财务衡量的是不同的事物。

segments.src: This article looks at what the headline figure captures, what tends to drive it, and why it can diverge from everyday experience.
segments.tr: 本文将探讨头条数据反映了什么、通常是什么在推动它，以及为什么它会与日常感受发生偏离。

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *本文仅供一般信息参考。

segments.src: It is not investment, tax or financial advice.*
segments.tr: 不构成投资、税务或财务建议。*

segments.src: ## What the 3.4% Actually Means
segments.tr: ## 3.4% 究竟意味着什么

segments.src: Gross domestic product is the total value of goods and services produced in the country over a period.
segments.tr: 国内生产总值（GDP）是指一个国家或地区在一定时期内生产的所有最终商品和服务的总价值。

segments.src: Government statisticians report the quarterly change as an **annualized** rate.
segments.tr: 政府统计人员将季度变化报告为**按年率计算（annualized）**的增长率。

segments.src: That is the pace the economy would reach if the quarter's growth continued for a full year.
segments.tr: 这是指如果该季度的增长速度维持一整年，经济所能达到的增速。

segments.src: A 3.4% reading does not mean the economy grew 3.4% in three months.
segments.tr: 3.4% 的数据并不意味着经济在三个月内增长了 3.4%。

segments.src: It means it expanded at a pace that, sustained, would add up to 3.4% over twelve months.
segments.tr: 它的意思是，如果这种扩张速度持续下去，十二个月积累下来将达到 3.4%。

segments.src: Three features of the figure matter for interpretation:
segments.tr: 理解这一数据时，有三个特征非常关键：

segments.src: - **It is an early estimate.** The first reading is based on incomplete data and is usually revised as more information arrives. Revisions can be meaningful.
segments.tr: - **这是初步估计。** 首次公布的数据基于不完整的数据，通常随着更多信息的获得而进行修正。修正幅度可能相当大。

segments.src: - **It is adjusted for inflation.** The headline is "real" GDP. It strips out price changes to show changes in output.
segments.tr: - **它经过了通胀调整。** 头条数据是“实际”GDP。它排除了价格变动，以反映产出的实际变化。

segments.src: - **It is an aggregate.** It tells you how big the total pie grew. It does not tell you who got the larger slices.
segments.tr: - **它是一个总量概念。** 它告诉你整体蛋糕增长了多少，但没有告诉你谁分到了更大的蛋糕。

segments.src: The acceleration from 2.2% to 3.4% suggests momentum improved.
segments.tr: 增速从 2.2% 提高到 3.4%，表明经济动能有所改善。

segments.src: Quarterly figures can be noisy, though, and analysts often look at several quarters together before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: 不过，季度数据可能存在波动噪音，分析师通常会在得出结论前综合观察多个季度。

segments.src: ## The Main Drivers
segments.tr: ## 主要推动因素

segments.src: GDP is built from a few components: consumer spending, business investment, government spending, and net trade.
segments.tr: GDP 由几个部分组成：消费者支出、企业投资、政府支出和净贸易。

segments.src: Which of these moved most is usually the key to understanding a quarter.
segments.tr: 其中哪一部分变化最大，通常是理解某一季度的关键。

segments.src: ### Consumers
segments.tr: ### 消费者

segments.src: Household spending is the largest piece of the economy, typically well over half of GDP.
segments.tr: 家庭支出是经济中最大的组成部分，通常占 GDP 的一半以上。

segments.src: When consumers keep buying services such as travel, health care and dining out, as well as goods, growth tends to hold up.
segments.tr: 当消费者持续购买旅游、医疗保健和餐饮等服务以及商品时，经济增长往往能保持稳定。

segments.src: Strong spending does not always mean households are comfortable, however.
segments.tr: 然而，强劲的支出并不总是意味着家庭感到宽裕。

segments.src: Some of it can reflect higher-income households spending freely.
segments.tr: 其中一部分可能反映了高收入家庭的高额消费。

segments.src: Some can reflect people drawing down savings or leaning on credit to keep up with higher prices.
segments.tr: 另一部分则可能反映了人们为了应对更高的物价而动用储蓄或依赖信贷。

segments.src: ### AI-Related Investment
segments.tr: ### AI 相关的投资

segments.src: Business investment has drawn particular attention because of heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
segments.tr: 由于在人工智能基础设施上的巨额支出，企业投资吸引了特别的关注。

segments.src: Data centers, computing hardware, software and the power and construction work that support them all count as investment in GDP.
segments.tr: 数据中心、计算硬件、软件以及支持它们的电力和建造工程，都被计入 GDP 的投资项中。

segments.src: This spending can lift the headline figure noticeably.
segments.tr: 这种支出可以明显拉高头条数据。

segments.src: It is also concentrated in a relatively small number of companies and industries.
segments.tr: 它也集中在相对少数的公司和行业中。

segments.src: A boom in server and data-center building can raise GDP without immediately changing the experience of a typical worker or renter.
segments.tr: 服务器和数据中心建设的繁荣可以提高 GDP，但不会立即改变普通工人或租房者的日常体验。

segments.src: ### Trade
segments.tr: ### 贸易

segments.src: Net exports are one of the more volatile pieces of the report.
segments.tr: 净出口是报告中最具波动性的部分之一。

segments.src: Imports subtract from GDP and exports add to it.
segments.tr: 进口会减少 GDP，而出口会增加 GDP。

segments.src: Swings in shipping, tariffs, inventory decisions and timing can move this component sharply from one quarter to the next.
segments.tr: 航运、关税、库存决策和时间安排的波动可能会使这一组成部分在不同季度间大幅变动。

segments.src: A big shift in trade can make the headline number look stronger or weaker than the underlying demand.
segments.tr: 贸易的大幅转变可能会使头条数据看起来比基础需求更强劲或更弱。

segments.src: For that reason, many economists also watch measures that strip out trade and inventories to get a cleaner read on domestic demand.
segments.tr: 出于这个原因，许多经济学家还会观察扣除贸易和库存后的指标，以更清晰地了解国内需求。

segments.src: ### Government and Inventories
segments.tr: ### 政府与库存

segments.src: Government spending and changes in business inventories also contribute.
segments.tr: 政府支出和企业库存的变化也有所贡献。

segments.src: Inventory swings in particular tend to reverse, so they can flatter one quarter and drag on the next.
segments.tr: 尤其是库存的波动往往会发生逆转，因此它们可能会抬高某一个季度的表现，却给下一个季度带来拖累。

segments.src: ## Why It Can Still Feel Slower
segments.tr: ## 为什么感觉依然放缓

segments.src: If output is rising at a healthy clip, why do so many people feel stuck?
segments.tr: 如果产出在以健康的速度增长，为什么还有这么多人感到生活艰难？

segments.src: Several explanations are commonly offered by economists.
segments.tr: 经济学家通常会提出以下几种解释。

segments.src: Prices rise even when inflation cools.** Inflation measures how fast prices increase.
segments.tr: 即使通胀降温，物价依然上涨。** 通胀衡量的是价格上涨的速度。

segments.src: A slowing rate does not mean prices fall.
segments.tr: 增速放缓并不意味着价格下降。

segments.src: If the cost of food, housing or insurance jumped in earlier years, those higher levels remain.
segments.tr: 如果食品、住房或保险成本在前几年飙升，那些较高的价格水平依然存在。

segments.src: Households tend to judge the economy by the prices they see now, not by the pace of change.
segments.tr: 家庭往往根据他们现在看到的物价来判断经济，而不是根据价格变化的速度。

segments.src: Essentials weigh more than averages suggest.** Official inflation gauges average across many goods.
segments.tr: 必需品的权重超出了平均水平所反映的范围。** 官方通胀衡量指标是对多种商品进行平均。

segments.src: A household that spends a large share of its income on rent, groceries, childcare or health care may experience its own inflation rate as higher than the average.
segments.tr: 如果一个家庭将收入的大部分用于支付房租、食品杂货、育儿或医疗保健，他们感受到的个人通胀率可能会高于平均水平。

segments.src: Borrowing remains expensive.** Even if interest rates have eased from their peaks, mortgage, auto and credit-card costs can be well above where they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: 借贷成本依然昂贵。** 即使利率从高点回落，住房抵押贷款、汽车贷款和信用卡成本仍可能远高于几年前的水平。

segments.src: That limits what many households can afford, whatever the national growth rate says.
segments.tr: 无论国家经济增长率如何，这都限制了许多家庭的负担能力。

segments.src: Growth is not evenly shared.** An economy can expand while gains flow mostly to business owners, investors and higher earners.
segments.tr: 增长成果分配不均。** 经济可以扩张，而收益却主要流向企业所有者、投资者和高收入者。

segments.src: Wage growth that merely keeps pace with prices leaves little sense of progress.
segments.tr: 如果工资增长仅仅跟上物价上涨的步伐，人们几乎体会不到生活水平的提高。

segments.src: Jobs and confidence are separate from output.** Growth can be strong while hiring slows or workers worry about job security.
segments.tr: 就业与信心独立于经济产出之外。** 经济增长可能强劲，但招聘放缓或工人对工作稳定性感到担忧。

segments.src: Perceptions of the labor market often shape sentiment more than GDP does.
segments.tr: 对劳动力市场的看法往往比 GDP 更能影响情绪。

segments.src: GDP is not a measure of well-being.** It counts production, not savings, debt, housing affordability or financial stress.
segments.tr: GDP 并不是衡量幸福感的指标。** 它统计的是生产量，而不是储蓄、债务、住房负担能力或财务压力。

segments.src: A country can post strong GDP while many individuals feel squeezed.
segments.tr: 一个国家可以在许多个人感到手头拮据的同时公布强劲的 GDP 数据。

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 下一步需要关注什么

segments.src: A single quarter does not settle the question.
segments.tr: 单一季度的数据并不能定论。

segments.src: These indicators can help put the 3.4% figure in context:
segments.tr: 以下指标有助于结合背景理解 3.4% 这一数据：

segments.src: - **Revisions to the GDP estimate**, which can change the story.
segments.tr: - **GDP 估算数据的修正**，这可能会改变整体结论。

segments.src: - **Real disposable income**, meaning income after taxes and inflation, which says more about household capacity than GDP does.
segments.tr: - **实际可支配收入**，即扣除税收和通胀后的收入，它比 GDP 更能说明家庭的能力。

segments.src: - **Wage growth compared with price growth**, since the gap between the two determines whether paychecks stretch further.
segments.tr: - **工资增长与价格增长的对比**，因为两者的差距决定了工资是否更加耐用。

segments.src: - **Labor market data**, including hiring, unemployment and job openings.
segments.tr: - **劳动力市场数据**，包括招聘量、失业率和职位空缺。

segments.src: - **Business investment outside the AI sector**, to see whether growth is broad or narrow.
segments.tr: - **AI 领域之外的企业投资**，以观察增长是广泛的还是狭隘的。

segments.src: - **Consumer sentiment surveys**, which capture how people feel, not only what they spend.
segments.tr: - **消费者信心指数调查**，它反映了人们的感受，而不仅仅是他们的支出。

segments.src: ## A Practical Takeaway for Households
segments.tr: ## 给家庭的实用建议

segments.src: National statistics are useful for understanding the economy's direction.
segments.tr: 国家统计数据有助于理解经济的发展方向。

segments.src: They are a poor guide to your own situation.
segments.tr: 但在衡量个人状况方面，它们并不是一个好的参考。

segments.src: A few general habits can help you separate the headlines from your own finances:
segments.tr: 几个一般的习惯可以帮助你将新闻头条与个人财务分离开来：

segments.src: - Track your own budget, especially the categories that have risen fastest.
segments.tr: - 追踪你自己的预算，特别是上涨最快的消费类别。

segments.src: - Compare your income growth with the prices you actually pay.
segments.tr: - 将你的收入增长与你实际支付的价格进行比较。

segments.src: - Review variable-rate debt and think about what a change in rates would mean for you.
segments.tr: - 审查浮动利率债务，并思考利率变化对你意味着什么。

segments.src: - Keep an emergency cushion if you can, since a strong economy does not guarantee job stability.
segments.tr: - 如果可以，保持一份应急缓冲资金，因为强劲的经济并不保证工作的稳定性。

segments.src: - Treat any single data release as one data point, not a forecast.
segments.tr: - 将任何单一的数据发布视为一个数据点，而不是预测。

segments.src: ## Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 总结

segments.src: A 3.4% annualized growth rate points to an economy with real momentum, helped by consumer spending, heavy AI-related investment and shifts in trade.
segments.tr: 3.4% 的按年率计算增长率表明经济具有真正的增长动能，这得益于消费者支出、强劲的 AI 相关投资以及贸易的转变。

segments.src: But GDP measures total output.
segments.tr: 但 GDP 衡量的是总产出。

segments.src: It does not measure how comfortable families feel after paying for housing, food and debt.
segments.tr: 它并不衡量家庭在支付了住房、食物和债务后的舒适程度。

segments.src: The gap between a strong headline and a tight household budget is not a contradiction.
segments.tr: 强劲的头条数据与紧绷的家庭预算之间的差距并不是矛盾。

segments.src: It reflects the difference between how much an economy produces and how that production, and the price of living, show up in daily life.
segments.tr: 它反映了一个经济体的生产总量，与该生产成果及生活成本在日常生活中如何呈现之间的差异。

segments.tr: *引用的数据反映了第三季度的最初估算，可能会进行修正。

segments.src: Readers should consult official sources, such as the Bureau of Economic Analysis, for the latest data.*
segments.tr: 读者应查阅官方来源（如 Bureau of Economic Analysis）以获取最新数据。*

segments.src: Three features of the figure matter for interpretation:
segments.tr: आंकड़े की व्याख्या के लिए तीन विशेषताएं मायने रखती हैं:

segments.src: - **It is an early estimate.** The first reading is based on incomplete data and is usually revised as more information arrives. Revisions can be meaningful.
segments.tr: - **यह एक प्रारंभिक अनुमान है।** पहली रीडिंग अधूरे डेटा पर आधारित होती है और आमतौर पर अधिक जानकारी आने पर इसे संशोधित किया जाता है। संशोधन महत्वपूर्ण हो सकते हैं।

segments.src: - **It is adjusted for inflation.** The headline is "real" GDP. It strips out price changes to show changes in output.
segments.tr: - **इसे मुद्रास्फीति के लिए समायोजित किया गया है।** मुख्य आंकड़ा "वास्तविक" जीडीपी है। यह उत्पादन में बदलाव दिखाने के लिए कीमतों में बदलाव को हटा देता है।

segments.src: - **It is an aggregate.** It tells you how big the total pie grew. It does not tell you who got the larger slices.
segments.tr: - **यह एक कुल योग है।** यह आपको बताता है कि कुल पाई कितनी बड़ी हो गई। यह आपको यह नहीं बताता कि बड़े हिस्से किसे मिले।

segments.src: The acceleration from 2.2% to 3.4% suggests momentum improved.
segments.tr: 2.2% से 3.4% तक की तेजी से पता चलता है कि गति में सुधार हुआ है।

segments.src: Quarterly figures can be noisy, though, and analysts often look at several quarters together before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: हालाँकि, तिमाही आंकड़े शोर भरे हो सकते हैं, और विश्लेषक निष्कर्ष निकालने से पहले अक्सर कई तिमाहियों को एक साथ देखते हैं।

segments.src: ## The Main Drivers
segments.tr: ## मुख्य चालक

segments.src: GDP is built from a few components: consumer spending, business investment, government spending, and net trade.
segments.tr: जीडीपी कुछ घटकों से बनी है: उपभोक्ता खर्च, व्यावसायिक निवेश, सरकारी खर्च और शुद्ध व्यापार।

segments.src: Which of these moved most is usually the key to understanding a quarter.
segments.tr: इनमें से कौन सा सबसे अधिक बढ़ा, यह आमतौर पर एक तिमाही को समझने की कुंजी है।

segments.src: ### Consumers
segments.tr: ### उपभोक्ता

segments.src: Household spending is the largest piece of the economy, typically well over half of GDP.
segments.tr: घरेलू खर्च अर्थव्यवस्था का सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा है, जो आमतौर पर जीडीपी के आधे से अधिक होता है।

segments.src: When consumers keep buying services such as travel, health care and dining out, as well as goods, growth tends to hold up.
segments.tr: जब उपभोक्ता यात्रा, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल और बाहर खाना खाने जैसी सेवाओं के साथ-साथ वस्तुओं को खरीदना जारी रखते हैं, तो विकास दर बनी रहती है।

segments.src: Strong spending does not always mean households are comfortable, however.
segments.tr: हालाँकि, मजबूत खर्च का मतलब हमेशा यह नहीं होता कि परिवार आरामदायक स्थिति में हैं।

segments.src: Some of it can reflect higher-income households spending freely.
segments.tr: इसका कुछ हिस्सा उच्च आय वाले परिवारों के खुलकर खर्च करने को दर्शा सकता है।

segments.src: Some can reflect people drawing down savings or leaning on credit to keep up with higher prices.
segments.tr: कुछ हिस्सा लोगों द्वारा बचत कम करने या बढ़ती कीमतों के साथ तालमेल बिठाने के लिए क्रेडिट पर निर्भर रहने को दर्शा सकता है।

segments.src: ### AI-Related Investment
segments.tr: ### एआई-संबंधित निवेश

segments.src: Business investment has drawn particular attention because of heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
segments.tr: व्यावसायिक निवेश ने कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (एआई) बुनियादी ढांचे पर भारी खर्च के कारण विशेष ध्यान आकर्षित किया है।

segments.src: Data centers, computing hardware, software and the power and construction work that support them all count as investment in GDP.
segments.tr: डेटा सेंटर, कंप्यूटिंग हार्डवेयर, सॉफ्टवेयर और उन्हें समर्थन देने वाले बिजली और निर्माण कार्य सभी जीडीपी में निवेश के रूप में गिने जाते हैं।

segments.src: This spending can lift the headline figure noticeably.
segments.tr: यह खर्च मुख्य आंकड़े को काफी बढ़ा सकता है।

segments.src: It is also concentrated in a relatively small number of companies and industries.
segments.tr: यह अपेक्षाकृत कम संख्या में कंपनियों और उद्योगों में केंद्रित भी है।

segments.src: A boom in server and data-center building can raise GDP without immediately changing the experience of a typical worker or renter.
segments.tr: सर्वर और डेटा-सेंटर निर्माण में उछाल एक सामान्य कर्मचारी या किराएदार के अनुभव को तुरंत बदले बिना जीडीपी बढ़ा सकता है।

segments.src: ### Trade
segments.tr: ### व्यापार

segments.src: Net exports are one of the more volatile pieces of the report.
segments.tr: शुद्ध निर्यात रिपोर्ट के अधिक अस्थिर हिस्सों में से एक है।

segments.src: Imports subtract from GDP and exports add to it.
segments.tr: आयात जीडीपी से घटते हैं और निर्यात इसमें जुड़ते हैं।

segments.src: Swings in shipping, tariffs, inventory decisions and timing can move this component sharply from one quarter to the next.
segments.tr: शिपिंग, टैरिफ, इन्वेंट्री निर्णयों और समय में बदलाव इस घटक को एक तिमाही से दूसरी तिमाही में तेजी से बदल सकते हैं।

segments.src: A big shift in trade can make the headline number look stronger or weaker than the underlying demand.
segments.tr: व्यापार में एक बड़ा बदलाव मुख्य संख्या को अंतर्निहित मांग से अधिक मजबूत या कमजोर दिखा सकता है।

segments.src: For that reason, many economists also watch measures that strip out trade and inventories to get a cleaner read on domestic demand.
segments.tr: इस कारण से, कई अर्थशास्त्री घरेलू मांग पर स्पष्ट नजर रखने के लिए व्यापार और इन्वेंट्री को हटाने वाले उपायों को भी देखते हैं।

segments.src: ### Government and Inventories
segments.tr: ### सरकार और इन्वेंट्री

segments.src: Government spending and changes in business inventories also contribute.
segments.tr: सरकारी खर्च और व्यावसायिक इन्वेंट्री में बदलाव भी योगदान करते हैं।

segments.src: Inventory swings in particular tend to reverse, so they can flatter one quarter and drag on the next.
segments.tr: इन्वेंट्री में उतार-चढ़ाव विशेष रूप से उलट जाते हैं, इसलिए वे एक तिमाही को बेहतर दिखा सकते हैं और अगली तिमाही पर बोझ डाल सकते हैं।

segments.src: ## Why It Can Still Feel Slower
segments.tr: ## यह अभी भी धीमा क्यों महसूस हो सकता है

segments.src: If output is rising at a healthy clip, why do so many people feel stuck?
segments.tr: यदि उत्पादन स्वस्थ गति से बढ़ रहा है, तो इतने सारे लोग फंसा हुआ क्यों महसूस करते हैं?

segments.src: Several explanations are commonly offered by economists.
segments.tr: अर्थशास्त्रियों द्वारा आमतौर पर कई स्पष्टीकरण दिए जाते हैं।

segments.src: Prices rise even when inflation cools.** Inflation measures how fast prices increase.
segments.tr: मुद्रास्फीति कम होने पर भी कीमतें बढ़ती हैं।** मुद्रास्फीति मापती है कि कीमतें कितनी तेजी से बढ़ती हैं।

segments.src: A slowing rate does not mean prices fall.
segments.tr: धीमी दर का मतलब यह नहीं है कि कीमतें गिरती हैं।

segments.src: If the cost of food, housing or insurance jumped in earlier years, those higher levels remain.
segments.tr: यदि भोजन, आवास या बीमा की लागत पिछले वर्षों में बढ़ी है, तो वे उच्च स्तर बने रहते हैं।

segments.src: Households tend to judge the economy by the prices they see now, not by the pace of change.
segments.tr: परिवार अर्थव्यवस्था को उन कीमतों से आंकते हैं जो वे अब देखते हैं, न कि बदलाव की गति से।

segments.src: Essentials weigh more than averages suggest.** Official inflation gauges average across many goods.
segments.tr: आवश्यक वस्तुएं औसत से अधिक भारी पड़ती हैं।** आधिकारिक मुद्रास्फीति गेज कई वस्तुओं का औसत निकालते हैं।

segments.src: A household that spends a large share of its income on rent, groceries, childcare or health care may experience its own inflation rate as higher than the average.
segments.tr: एक परिवार जो अपनी आय का एक बड़ा हिस्सा किराए, किराने, चाइल्डकैअर या स्वास्थ्य देखभाल पर खर्च करता है, वह अपनी मुद्रास्फीति दर को औसत से अधिक अनुभव कर सकता है।

segments.src: Borrowing remains expensive.** Even if interest rates have eased from their peaks, mortgage, auto and credit-card costs can be well above where they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: उधार लेना महंगा बना हुआ है।** भले ही ब्याज दरें अपने चरम से कम हो गई हों, मॉर्गेज, ऑटो और क्रेडिट-कार्ड की लागत कुछ साल पहले की तुलना में काफी अधिक हो सकती है।

segments.src: That limits what many households can afford, whatever the national growth rate says.
segments.tr: यह सीमित करता है कि कई परिवार क्या खर्च कर सकते हैं, चाहे राष्ट्रीय विकास दर कुछ भी कहे।

segments.src: Growth is not evenly shared.** An economy can expand while gains flow mostly to business owners, investors and higher earners.
segments.tr: विकास समान रूप से साझा नहीं किया जाता है।** एक अर्थव्यवस्था का विस्तार हो सकता है जबकि लाभ मुख्य रूप से व्यवसाय के मालिकों, निवेशकों और उच्च कमाई करने वालों तक पहुंचता है।

segments.src: Wage growth that merely keeps pace with prices leaves little sense of progress.
segments.tr: वेतन वृद्धि जो केवल कीमतों के साथ तालमेल रखती है, प्रगति का बहुत कम अहसास कराती है।

segments.src: Jobs and confidence are separate from output.** Growth can be strong while hiring slows or workers worry about job security.
segments.tr: नौकरियां और विश्वास उत्पादन से अलग हैं।** विकास मजबूत हो सकता है जबकि भर्ती धीमी हो जाती है या श्रमिक नौकरी की सुरक्षा को लेकर चिंतित रहते हैं।

segments.src: Perceptions of the labor market often shape sentiment more than GDP does.
segments.tr: श्रम बाजार की धारणाएं अक्सर जीडीपी की तुलना में भावना को अधिक आकार देती हैं।

segments.src: GDP is not a measure of well-being.** It counts production, not savings, debt, housing affordability or financial stress.
segments.tr: जीडीपी कल्याण का माप नहीं है।** यह उत्पादन को गिनता है, बचत, ऋण, आवास सामर्थ्य या वित्तीय तनाव को नहीं।

segments.src: A country can post strong GDP while many individuals feel squeezed.
segments.tr: एक देश मजबूत जीडीपी पोस्ट कर सकता है जबकि कई व्यक्ति दबाव महसूस करते हैं।

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## आगे क्या देखना है

segments.src: A single quarter does not settle the question.
segments.tr: एक तिमाही सवाल का समाधान नहीं करती है।

segments.src: These indicators can help put the 3.4% figure in context:
segments.tr: ये संकेतक 3.4% के आंकड़े को संदर्भ में रखने में मदद कर सकते हैं:

segments.src: - **Revisions to the GDP estimate**, which can change the story.
segments.tr: - **जीडीपी अनुमान में संशोधन**, जो कहानी बदल सकते हैं।

segments.src: - **Real disposable income**, meaning income after taxes and inflation, which says more about household capacity than GDP does.
segments.tr: - **वास्तविक डिस्पोजेबल आय**, यानी करों और मुद्रास्फीति के बाद की आय, जो जीडीपी की तुलना में घरेलू क्षमता के बारे में अधिक बताती है।

segments.src: - **Wage growth compared with price growth**, since the gap between the two determines whether paychecks stretch further.
segments.tr: - **कीमत वृद्धि की तुलना में वेतन वृद्धि**, क्योंकि दोनों के बीच का अंतर यह निर्धारित करता है कि वेतन कितना आगे तक जाता है।

segments.src: - **Labor market data**, including hiring, unemployment and job openings.
segments.tr: - **श्रम बाजार डेटा**, जिसमें भर्ती, बेरोजगारी और नौकरी के अवसर शामिल हैं।

segments.src: - **Business investment outside the AI sector**, to see whether growth is broad or narrow.
segments.tr: - **एआई क्षेत्र के बाहर व्यावसायिक निवेश**, यह देखने के लिए कि विकास व्यापक है या संकीर्ण।

segments.src: - **Consumer sentiment surveys**, which capture how people feel, not only what they spend.
segments.tr: - **उपभोक्ता भावना सर्वेक्षण**, जो यह पकड़ते हैं कि लोग कैसा महसूस करते हैं, न कि केवल वे क्या खर्च करते हैं।

segments.src: ## A Practical Takeaway for Households
segments.tr: ## परिवारों के लिए एक व्यावहारिक निष्कर्ष

segments.src: National statistics are useful for understanding the economy's direction.
segments.tr: राष्ट्रीय आंकड़े अर्थव्यवस्था की दिशा समझने के लिए उपयोगी हैं।

segments.src: They are a poor guide to your own situation.
segments.tr: वे आपकी अपनी स्थिति के लिए खराब मार्गदर्शक हैं।

segments.src: A few general habits can help you separate the headlines from your own finances:
segments.tr: कुछ सामान्य आदतें आपको सुर्खियों को अपने वित्त से अलग करने में मदद कर सकती हैं:

segments.src: - Track your own budget, especially the categories that have risen fastest.
segments.tr: - अपने बजट को ट्रैक करें, विशेष रूप से उन श्रेणियों को जो सबसे तेजी से बढ़ी हैं।

segments.src: - Compare your income growth with the prices you actually pay.
segments.tr: - अपनी आय वृद्धि की तुलना उन कीमतों से करें जो आप वास्तव में चुकाते हैं।

segments.src: - Review variable-rate debt and think about what a change in rates would mean for you.
segments.tr: - परिवर्तनीय-दर ऋण की समीक्षा करें और सोचें कि दरों में बदलाव का आपके लिए क्या मतलब होगा।

segments.src: - Keep an emergency cushion if you can, since a strong economy does not guarantee job stability.
segments.tr: - यदि आप कर सकते हैं तो एक आपातकालीन कुशन रखें, क्योंकि एक मजबूत अर्थव्यवस्था नौकरी की स्थिरता की गारंटी नहीं देती है।

segments.src: - Treat any single data release as one data point, not a forecast.
segments.tr: - किसी भी एकल डेटा रिलीज को एक डेटा बिंदु के रूप में मानें, न कि पूर्वानुमान के रूप में।

segments.src: ## Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## निष्कर्ष

segments.src: A 3.4% annualized growth rate points to an economy with real momentum, helped by consumer spending, heavy AI-related investment and shifts in trade.
segments.tr: 3.4% की वार्षिक विकास दर एक वास्तविक गति वाली अर्थव्यवस्था की ओर इशारा करती है, जिसे उपभोक्ता खर्च, भारी एआई-संबंधित निवेश और व्यापार में बदलाव से मदद मिली है।

segments.src: But GDP measures total output.
segments.tr: लेकिन जीडीपी कुल उत्पादन को मापता है।

segments.src: It does not measure how comfortable families feel after paying for housing, food and debt.
segments.tr: यह यह नहीं मापता है कि आवास, भोजन और ऋण के लिए भुगतान करने के बाद परिवार कितना आरामदायक महसूस करते हैं।

segments.src: The gap between a strong headline and a tight household budget is not a contradiction.
segments.tr: एक मजबूत हेडलाइन और तंग घरेलू बजट के बीच का अंतर कोई विरोधाभास नहीं है।

segments.src: It reflects the difference between how much an economy produces and how that production, and the price of living, show up in daily life.
segments.tr: यह इस बात के अंतर को दर्शाता है कि एक अर्थव्यवस्था कितना उत्पादन करती है और वह उत्पादन, और जीवन की कीमत, दैनिक जीवन में कैसे दिखाई देते हैं।

es.title: Crecimiento del 3.4%, ¿entonces por qué se siente más lento? Leyendo el reporte del PIB del tercer trimestre

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: La

segments.src: economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% in the second.
segments.tr: economía de EE. UU. creció a una tasa anualizada del 3.4% en el tercer trimestre, frente al 2.2% del segundo.

segments.src: By the usual yardsticks, that is a solid number.
segments.tr: Según los estándares habituales, es una cifra sólida.

segments.src: Yet plenty of households say they feel no stronger, because grocery bills, rent, insurance and borrowing costs still weigh on their budgets.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, muchos hogares dicen que no se sienten más fuertes, porque las facturas de comestibles, el alquiler, los seguros y los costos de endeudamiento aún pesan sobre sus presupuestos.

segments.src: Both things can be true.
segments.tr: Ambas cosas pueden ser ciertas.

segments.src: GDP and a family's finances measure different things.
segments.tr: El PIB y las finanzas de una familia miden cosas diferentes.

segments.src: This article looks at what the headline figure captures, what tends to drive it, and why it can diverge from everyday experience.
segments.tr: Este artículo analiza lo que capta la cifra principal, lo que tiende a impulsarla y por qué puede diferir de la experiencia cotidiana.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *Este artículo es solo para información general.

segments.src: It is not investment, tax or financial advice.*
segments.tr: No constituye asesoramiento de inversión, fiscal ni financiero.*

segments.src: ## What the 3.4% Actually Means
segments.tr: ## Lo que realmente significa el 3.4%

segments.src: Gross domestic product is the total value of goods and services produced in the country over a period.
segments.tr: El producto interno bruto es el valor total de los bienes y servicios producidos en el país durante un período.

segments.src: Government statisticians report the quarterly change as an **annualized** rate.
segments.tr: Los estadísticos del gobierno informan el cambio trimestral como una tasa **anualizada**.

segments.src: That is the pace the economy would reach if the quarter's growth continued for a full year.
segments.tr: Ese es el ritmo que alcanzaría la economía si el crecimiento del trimestre continuara durante todo un año.

segments.src: A 3.4% reading does not mean the economy grew 3.4% in three months.
segments.tr: Una lectura del 3.4% no significa que la economía creció un 3.4% en tres meses.

segments.src: It means it expanded at a pace that, sustained, would add up to 3.4% over twelve months.
segments.tr: Significa que se expandió a un ritmo que, sostenido, sumaría un 3.4% durante doce meses.

segments.src: Three features of the figure matter for interpretation:
segments.tr: Tres características de la cifra importan para su interpretación:

segments.src: - **It is an early estimate.** The first reading is based on incomplete data and is usually revised as more information arrives. Revisions can be meaningful.
segments.tr: - **Es una estimación temprana.** La primera lectura se basa en datos incompletos y suele revisarse a medida que llega más información. Las revisiones pueden ser significativas.

segments.src: - **It is adjusted for inflation.** The headline is "real" GDP. It strips out price changes to show changes in output.
segments.tr: - **Está ajustada por inflación.** El titular es el PIB "real". Elimina los cambios de precios para mostrar los cambios en la producción.

segments.src: - **It is an aggregate.** It tells you how big the total pie grew. It does not tell you who got the larger slices.
segments.tr: - **Es un agregado.** Te dice cuánto creció el pastel total. No te dice quién obtuvo las porciones más grandes.

segments.src: The acceleration from 2.2% to 3.4% suggests momentum improved.
segments.tr: La aceleración del 2.2% al 3.4% sugiere que el impulso mejoró.

segments.src: Quarterly figures can be noisy, though, and analysts often look at several quarters together before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, las cifras trimestrales pueden ser volátiles, y los analistas suelen observar varios trimestres juntos antes de sacar conclusiones.

segments.src: ## The Main Drivers
segments.tr: ## Los principales motores

segments.src: GDP is built from a few components: consumer spending, business investment, government spending, and net trade.
segments.tr: El PIB se construye a partir de algunos componentes: gasto de los consumidores, inversión empresarial, gasto público y comercio neto.

segments.src: Which of these moved most is usually the key to understanding a quarter.
segments.tr: Cuál de estos se movió más suele ser la clave para entender un trimestre.

segments.src: ### Consumers
segments.tr: ### Consumidores

segments.src: Household spending is the largest piece of the economy, typically well over half of GDP.
segments.tr: El gasto de los hogares es la mayor parte de la economía, típicamente muy por encima de la mitad del PIB.

segments.src: When consumers keep buying services such as travel, health care and dining out, as well as goods, growth tends to hold up.
segments.tr: Cuando los consumidores siguen comprando servicios como viajes, atención médica y salir a cenar, así como bienes, el crecimiento tiende a sostenerse.

segments.src: Strong spending does not always mean households are comfortable, however.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, un gasto fuerte no siempre significa que los hogares estén cómodos.

segments.src: Some of it can reflect higher-income households spending freely.
segments.tr: Parte de esto puede reflejar que los hogares de mayores ingresos gastan libremente.

segments.src: Some can reflect people drawing down savings or leaning on credit to keep up with higher prices.
segments.tr: Parte puede reflejar a personas que agotan sus ahorros o recurren al crédito para mantenerse al día con los precios más altos.

segments.src: ### AI-Related Investment
segments.tr: ### Inversión relacionada con la IA

segments.src: Business investment has drawn particular attention because of heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
segments.tr: La inversión empresarial ha atraído una atención particular debido al fuerte gasto en infraestructura de inteligencia artificial.

segments.src: Data centers, computing hardware, software and the power and construction work that support them all count as investment in GDP.
segments.tr: Los centros de datos, el hardware informático, el software y el trabajo de energía y construcción que los respaldan cuentan como inversión en el PIB.

segments.src: This spending can lift the headline figure noticeably.
segments.tr: Este gasto puede elevar la cifra principal de manera notable.

segments.src: It is also concentrated in a relatively small number of companies and industries.
segments.tr: También está concentrado en un número relativamente pequeño de empresas e industrias.

segments.src: A boom in server and data-center building can raise GDP without immediately changing the experience of a typical worker or renter.
segments.tr: Un auge en la construcción de servidores y centros de datos puede elevar el PIB sin cambiar inmediatamente la experiencia de un trabajador o inquilino típico.

segments.src: ### Trade
segments.tr: ### Comercio

segments.src: Net exports are one of the more volatile pieces of the report.
segments.tr: Las exportaciones netas son una de las partes más volátiles del informe.

segments.src: Imports subtract from GDP and exports add to it.
segments.tr: Las importaciones restan del PIB y las exportaciones suman a él.

segments.src: Swings in shipping, tariffs, inventory decisions and timing can move this component sharply from one quarter to the next.
segments.tr: Los cambios en el transporte marítimo, aranceles, decisiones de inventario y plazos pueden mover este componente bruscamente de un trimestre a otro.

segments.src: A big shift in trade can make the headline number look stronger or weaker than the underlying demand.
segments.tr: Un gran cambio en el comercio puede hacer que la cifra principal parezca más fuerte o más débil que la demanda subyacente.

segments.src: For that reason, many economists also watch measures that strip out trade and inventories to get a cleaner read on domestic demand.
segments.tr: Por esa razón, muchos economistas también observan medidas que excluyen el comercio y los inventarios para obtener una lectura más limpia de la demanda interna.

segments.src: ### Government and Inventories
segments.tr: ### Gobierno e inventarios

segments.src: Government spending and changes in business inventories also contribute.
segments.tr: El gasto público y los cambios en los inventarios empresariales también contribuyen.

segments.src: Inventory swings in particular tend to reverse, so they can flatter one quarter and drag on the next.
segments.tr: Los cambios en los inventarios, en particular, tienden a revertirse, por lo que pueden favorecer a un trimestre y frenar al siguiente.

segments.src: ## Why It Can Still Feel Slower
segments.tr: ## Por qué aún puede sentirse más lento

segments.src: If output is rising at a healthy clip, why do so many people feel stuck?
segments.tr: Si la producción está aumentando a un ritmo saludable, ¿por qué tanta gente se siente estancada?

segments.src: Several explanations are commonly offered by economists.
segments.tr: Los economistas suelen ofrecer varias explicaciones.

segments.src: Prices rise even when inflation cools.** Inflation measures how fast prices increase.
segments.tr: Los precios suben incluso cuando la inflación se enfría.** La inflación mide qué tan rápido aumentan los precios.

segments.src: A slowing rate does not mean prices fall.
segments.tr: Una tasa de desaceleración no significa que los precios bajen.

segments.src: If the cost of food, housing or insurance jumped in earlier years, those higher levels remain.
segments.tr: Si el costo de los alimentos, la vivienda o los seguros saltó en años anteriores, esos niveles más altos se mantienen.

segments.src: Households tend to judge the economy by the prices they see now, not by the pace of change.
segments.tr: Los hogares tienden a juzgar la economía por los precios que ven ahora, no por el ritmo de cambio.

segments.src: Essentials weigh more than averages suggest.** Official inflation gauges average across many goods.
segments.tr: Los productos esenciales pesan más de lo que sugieren los promedios.** Los indicadores oficiales de inflación promedian entre muchos bienes.

segments.src: A household that spends a large share of its income on rent, groceries, childcare or health care may experience its own inflation rate as higher than the average.
segments.tr: Un hogar que gasta una gran parte de sus ingresos en alquiler, comestibles, cuidado infantil o atención médica puede experimentar su propia tasa de inflación como superior al promedio.

segments.src: Borrowing remains expensive.** Even if interest rates have eased from their peaks, mortgage, auto and credit-card costs can be well above where they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: El endeudamiento sigue siendo caro.** Incluso si las tasas de interés se han relajado desde sus picos, los costos de hipotecas, automóviles y tarjetas de crédito pueden estar muy por encima de lo que estaban hace unos años.

segments.src: That limits what many households can afford, whatever the national growth rate says.
segments.tr: Eso limita lo que muchos hogares pueden permitirse, independientemente de lo que diga la tasa de crecimiento nacional.

segments.src: Growth is not evenly shared.** An economy can expand while gains flow mostly to business owners, investors and higher earners.
segments.tr: El crecimiento no se comparte de manera equitativa.** Una economía puede expandirse mientras las ganancias fluyen principalmente hacia los dueños de negocios, inversores y personas con mayores ingresos.

segments.src: Wage growth that merely keeps pace with prices leaves little sense of progress.
segments.tr: Un crecimiento salarial que simplemente sigue el ritmo de los precios deja poca sensación de progreso.

segments.src: Jobs and confidence are separate from output.** Growth can be strong while hiring slows or workers worry about job security.
segments.tr: Los empleos y la confianza son independientes de la producción.** El crecimiento puede ser fuerte mientras la contratación se desacelera o los trabajadores se preocupan por la seguridad laboral.

segments.src: Perceptions of the labor market often shape sentiment more than GDP does.
segments.tr: Las percepciones del mercado laboral a menudo moldean el sentimiento más que el PIB.

segments.src: GDP is not a measure of well-being.** It counts production, not savings, debt, housing affordability or financial stress.
segments.tr: El PIB no es una medida de bienestar.** Cuenta la producción, no los ahorros, la deuda, la asequibilidad de la vivienda o el estrés financiero.

segments.src: A country can post strong GDP while many individuals feel squeezed.
segments.tr: Un país puede registrar un PIB fuerte mientras muchos individuos se sienten presionados.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Qué observar a continuación

segments.src: A single quarter does not settle the question.
segments.tr: Un solo trimestre no zanja la cuestión.

segments.src: These indicators can help put the 3.4% figure in context:
segments.tr: Estos indicadores pueden ayudar a poner la cifra del 3.4% en contexto:

segments.src: - **Revisions to the GDP estimate**, which can change the story.
segments.tr: - **Revisiones a la estimación del PIB**, que pueden cambiar la historia.

segments.src: - **Real disposable income**, meaning income after taxes and inflation, which says more about household capacity than GDP does.
segments.tr: - **Ingreso disponible real**, es decir, el ingreso después de impuestos e inflación, que dice más sobre la capacidad de los hogares que el PIB.

segments.src: - **Wage growth compared with price growth**, since the gap between the two determines whether paychecks stretch further.
segments.tr: - **Crecimiento salarial en comparación con el crecimiento de los precios**, ya que la brecha entre ambos determina si los cheques de pago rinden más.

segments.src: - **Labor market data**, including hiring, unemployment and job openings.
segments.tr: - **Datos del mercado laboral**, incluida la contratación, el desempleo y las ofertas de empleo.

segments.src: - **Business investment outside the AI sector**, to see whether growth is broad or narrow.
segments.tr: - **Inversión empresarial fuera del sector de la IA**, para ver si el crecimiento es amplio o estrecho.

segments.src: - **Consumer sentiment surveys**, which capture how people feel, not only what they spend.
segments.tr: - **Encuestas de sentimiento del consumidor**, que capturan cómo se siente la gente, no solo lo que gastan.

segments.src: ## A Practical Takeaway for Households
segments.tr: ## Una conclusión práctica para los hogares

segments.src: National statistics are useful for understanding the economy's direction.
segments.tr: Las estadísticas nacionales son útiles para entender la dirección de la economía.

segments.src: They are a poor guide to your own situation.
segments.tr: Son una guía pobre para tu propia situación.

segments.src: A few general habits can help you separate the headlines from your own finances:
segments.tr: Unos cuantos hábitos generales pueden ayudarte a separar los titulares de tus propias finanzas:

segments.src: - Track your own budget, especially the categories that have risen fastest.
segments.tr: - Lleva un registro de tu propio presupuesto, especialmente de las categorías que han subido más rápido.

segments.src: - Compare your income growth with the prices you actually pay.
segments.tr: - Compara el crecimiento de tus ingresos con los precios que realmente pagas.

segments.src: - Review variable-rate debt and think about what a change in rates would mean for you.
segments.tr: - Revisa la deuda de tasa variable y piensa en lo que significaría para ti un cambio en las tasas.

segments.src: - Keep an emergency cushion if you can, since a strong economy does not guarantee job stability.
segments.tr: - Mantén un fondo de emergencia si puedes, ya que una economía fuerte no garantiza la estabilidad laboral.

segments.src: - Treat any single data release as one data point, not a forecast.
segments.tr: - Trata cualquier publicación de datos individuales como un punto de datos, no como un pronóstico.

segments.src: ## Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## En resumen

segments.src: A 3.4% annualized growth rate points to an economy with real momentum, helped by consumer spending, heavy AI-related investment and shifts in trade.
segments.tr: Una tasa de crecimiento anualizada del 3.4% apunta a una economía con un impulso real, ayudada por el gasto de los consumidores, la fuerte inversión relacionada con la IA y los cambios en el comercio.

segments.src: But GDP measures total output.
segments.tr: Pero el PIB mide la producción total.

segments.src: It does not measure how comfortable families feel after paying for housing, food and debt.
segments.tr: No mide cuán cómodas se sienten las familias después de pagar por la vivienda, la comida y la deuda.

segments.src: The gap between a strong headline and a tight household budget is not a contradiction.
segments.tr: La brecha entre un titular fuerte y un presupuesto familiar ajustado no es una contradicción.

segments.src: It reflects the difference between how much an economy produces and how that production, and the price of living, show up in daily life.
segments.tr: Refleja la diferencia entre cuánto produce una economía y cómo esa producción, y el precio de la vida, se manifiestan en la vida diaria.

segments.src: *Figures cited reflect the initial third-quarter estimate and may be revised.
segments.tr: *Las cifras citadas reflejan la estimación inicial del tercer trimestre y pueden ser revisadas.

segments.src: Readers should consult official sources, such as the Bureau of Economic Analysis, for the latest data.*
segments.tr: Los lectores deben consultar fuentes oficiales, como la Oficina de Análisis Económico, para obtener los datos más recientes.*
